newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease as foreigners stay away.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease as foreigners stay away.

text.p: Slovenian shares dropped 1.88 percent on Tuesday and traders said the market was expected to continue its slide until foreign investors returned in force.

"Domestic investors do not have sufficient (financial) potential to sustain the current price level. If international investors keep away, shares could continue falling for several months," said Karmen Cerar, a trader at brokerage Poteza.
The SBI index fell 26.52 points to finish the session at 1,385.69, down 3.3 percent from last week's close.
The central bank three weeks ago ordered foreign investors to open custodian accounts with local banks if they wanted to trade in Slovenian securities.
Details of the accounts are still sketchy, but the cost of keeping them is expected to amount to about 12 percent of the total amount handled.
Since February 10 when the central bank made its move, the index has dropped 16.3 percent.
"Uncertainty on the market will prevail until banks clarify the costs of custodian accounts and amount of money they will be able to handle," said Crt Jakhel, a trader at brokerage Nika.
Overall 10 shares fell, two rose and 14 were untraded. Turnover fell to 76.3 million tolars from 84.1 million.
Bank SKB was the most active share, falling 1.95 percent to 57,850 tolars on volume of 436 shares, for total turnover of 25.7 million tolars.
The bank on Monday reported a 2.5-fold increase in 1996 net profit, boosted by improved interest margins and increased domestic and international business.
Brokerage Nika led the day's decliners, falling 4.08 percent to 3,600 tolars on volume of 2,432 shares for total turnover of 8.8 million.
Warehouse and shopping centre operator BTC was the biggest gainer, firming 3.31 percent to 13,430 tolars on volume of 628 shares for total turnover of 8.3 million tolars.
